findings.title: Vite serves private local files containing database credentials
findings.trigger: After documented local database initialization and pnpm dev, /@fs/<workspace-root>/.local/postgres/ownership.json falls inside Vite file allow rules. Runtime verification used only .local/review/public-canary.json containing a fake marker with mode0600; plain, raw, import and raw/import variants returned HTTP200. A different localhost browser origin received matching ACAO.
findings.actual: Private mode0600 .local JSON is served byte-for-byte by the dev server; transformed import responses also expose its content. A separate localhost origin receives read permission via matching ACAO. The same unprotected .local tree holds generated database password/root/port metadata. API middleware does not run on Vite file requests.
findings.expected: Private .local state, database credentials and local-only runtime/assets cannot be served by the development browser server.
dependencyEvidence: apps/web/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/config.js:25787-25812 default deny and workspace allow resolution
findings.recommendation: Constrain frontend/shared-package file serving and explicitly deny the entire private .local tree while retaining default secret-file protections. Add browser/dev-server regression coverage for benign private canaries including normal /@fs and raw/import variants, and validate expected frontend/shared package loading.
findings.testGap: Existing API security tests cover Express/Nest only and do not exercise Vite private-file serving.
